transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I came because I can’t get past this feeling that I’m dangerous somehow. Like I’m a disappointment. There was this near-miss, and I keep replaying it, like it proves I’m not cut out to be a nurse.

And I know people say mistakes happen, but it doesn’t feel like that. It feels like everyone would be better off if I just wasn’t… in the way. Sorry, I’m not explaining it right. I was thinking about my shift and then my instructor’s face, and it just keeps looping.
Have you had thoughts of harming yourself?

I… not like, I don’t have a plan or anything. I haven’t thought out a way to hurt myself.

It’s more like these thoughts keep coming up that maybe it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up, or if I could disappear so I wouldn’t mess anything up again. And then I feel guilty for even thinking that, because I know people have real problems, and my mom always says I overthink things—sorry, I’m getting off track. But yes, I’ve had those thoughts.
How long have you been feeling this way about being a disappointment and having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up?

I think… about a year and two months? It kind of started after I graduated high school and then jumped into college classes and working full-time at the clinic, which I thought I could handle because everyone else seems to just… do it.

At first I thought it was just stress from the schedule, like waking up early and trying to keep track of assignments and shifts, and my mom kept saying I just needed to get used to it. But it’s been there since then, that feeling like I’m falling behind or messing everything up. So… yeah, around a year and two months.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge when you're not thinking about the near-miss or your responsibilities as a nurse?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean… I know I get nervous when I’m thinking about the clinic stuff, or school, or whether I messed something up, but if you mean just sitting there for no reason feeling on edge… I don’t really know.

Sometimes I can’t tell what starts it, because I’ll be thinking about one thing and then it turns into another, like I’ll remember I forgot to text someone back and then suddenly I’m thinking about my whole life. Sorry. I guess I haven’t really noticed whether it happens separate from the nursing stuff.
Do you ever feel nervous or on edge without any particular reason or when you're not thinking about work or school?

I… I don’t know. I’m trying to think of a time when it’s just there without something causing it, but I guess I usually connect it to something after the fact, even if it’s small.

Like, I’ll feel weird and tense, and then I’ll be like, oh, maybe it’s because I didn’t finish that email or because I said something awkward earlier. But I don’t know if that counts as “no reason” or if I’m just finding a reason. Sorry, that probably doesn’t answer it very clearly.
Do you ever wake up feeling anxious or on edge without knowing why?

I don’t really know. Some mornings I wake up already kind of tense, but then I’ll immediately start thinking about what I have to do that day, or whether I forgot something, so it’s hard to tell if the anxiety was there first or if my brain just grabs onto something right away.

Like even before I’m fully awake I’ll think, did I set my alarm wrong, do I have class, am I supposed to be somewhere… and then it just turns into this whole thing. So I guess I haven’t noticed it happening with absolutely no reason. I’m not sure.
Do you feel anxious when you're doing something you enjoy and there's no pressure or stress involved?

I’m not really sure. I mean, if I’m doing something I actually like, like watching something or scrolling through little craft videos or whatever, I can still kind of drift into thinking about other things, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxious in that moment.

Sometimes I’ll start enjoying something and then remember I should be doing something else, and then it’s not really “no pressure” anymore, you know? Sorry, I feel like I’m answering around it. I guess I haven’t really noticed feeling anxious during something enjoyable if there’s truly nothing attached to it.
Do you feel anxious when you are alone with nothing to do?

I don’t know, honestly. If I’m alone with nothing to do, I usually find something to do pretty quickly, even if it’s just looking at my phone or reorganizing some random thing that doesn’t need reorganizing.

But if you mean just sitting there with no distractions… I don’t really do that much. It makes me feel kind of uncomfortable, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxious exactly. Sometimes I’ll start thinking about stuff I forgot, or like, little things I need to fix, and then it kind of goes from “nothing to do” to having a bunch of things in my head.

Sorry, that probably wasn’t a straight answer. I guess I haven’t really noticed it as anxiety for no reason when I’m just alone.
Do you often worry about things that are not related to your work or school?

Um… outside of school or work? I don’t know. I mean, I worry about random stuff, but it’s hard to separate because everything kind of connects back somehow. Like if I’m worried about money or my room being a mess, then that affects whether I can focus, and then it becomes school-related again.

Sometimes I’ll worry about little things like whether I said something weird to someone, or if I forgot to text back, but I don’t know if that counts as “often.” I guess I haven’t really kept track of it. Sorry, I’m kind of circling around the question.
Do you find yourself worrying about a wide range of everyday things, even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

I’m not totally sure. I do worry about everyday stuff sometimes, but “wide range” makes it sound really… constant, and I don’t know if that’s true for me.

Like, I can get stuck thinking about whether I handled some little thing right, but then sometimes I’m fine and distracted by something else. And then other times I’ll remember, like, laundry or an appointment or something I meant to do, and it spirals a little, but I don’t know if that’s worry for no obvious reason or just me remembering things at a bad time.

Sorry, I think I’m overexplaining. I guess I haven’t really noticed myself worrying about everything all the time for no reason.
Do you find yourself worrying about things even when everything in your life seems to be going well?

I don’t really know. I mean, when things are going well, I guess I still find little things to think about, but I’m not sure I’d call it worrying exactly.

Like sometimes even if nothing is actively wrong, I’ll start thinking about some random thing I need to handle, or whether I’m forgetting something. But then again, “everything going well” is kind of hard for me to judge, because there’s usually some little thing—like laundry or messages or whatever—that makes it feel not completely settled.

Sorry, I’m kind of drifting from the question. I don’t think I’ve clearly noticed myself worrying a lot when everything is fine.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things for a long time, even after you've tried to deal with them?

I’m not really sure. Sometimes I’ll keep thinking about something after I’ve already done what I’m supposed to do about it, like sending a message or checking something, but I don’t know if it’s “a long time.”

It kind of depends… like if I’m tired, everything sticks more, and then I’ll be thinking about it while I’m doing something totally unrelated, like making food or trying to clean, and then I forget what I was cleaning in the first place. Sorry, that’s not really the point.

I guess I haven’t noticed a clear pattern of worrying for a long time after dealing with things.
Do you find yourself continuing to worry about something even after you've resolved the issue?

I guess… not really in a way I can clearly point to. Sometimes after something is fixed, I’ll still think about it a little, like, “Did I do that right?” or I’ll replay a conversation, but then I’m also the kind of person who’ll remember I need to buy detergent and suddenly I’m thinking about three other things.

So I don’t know if that counts as continuing to worry after it’s resolved. I haven’t really noticed that being a big pattern for me.
Do you often find yourself worrying about the future in general?

I’m not sure. I mean, I think about the future sometimes, like what I’m supposed to be doing next or whether I’m behind, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m worrying about the future in general.

It’s more like… my mind jumps around. I’ll think about next week, and then suddenly I’m thinking about something I forgot to wash, or some form I need to deal with, and then I’m not even on the future anymore.

So, I guess I haven’t really noticed it as a big constant thing, if that makes sense.
Do you often find yourself thinking about potential problems or negative outcomes that could happen in the future?

I don’t really know. Sometimes I’ll think, like, “What if this goes wrong?” but then it kind of turns into thinking about something totally different, like whether I left laundry in the washer or if I answered someone’s text.

So… I can’t say I often sit there thinking through negative future outcomes. It’s more scattered than that, I think.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things in general, even when there's nothing specific going on?

I don’t think so… or I’m not sure. Like, I don’t usually sit there worrying when nothing is happening, at least not in a way I can clearly describe.

Sometimes my brain is just busy, like I’ll be thinking about one thing and then suddenly I’m remembering something from work or school or that I need to charge my phone, but I don’t know if that’s worry exactly. It’s more like noise in my head.

So… I haven’t really noticed myself worrying about things in general for no specific reason.
Have you been feeling this way consistently over the past year and two months, or have there been periods where your symptoms improved?

It’s been pretty consistent, I think… like, not exactly every single day the same, but this general feeling has been there for about a year and two months.

It kind of started after I graduated high school and then started college classes and working full-time at the clinic. I remember thinking I was just adjusting, because everyone says that first year is weird, and I bought all these notebooks like that would make me feel organized, but… yeah, it didn’t really just go away. There may have been better days, but I don’t think there was a real stretch where it actually improved.
Have your feelings of being a disappointment and thoughts of not wanting to wake up been present nearly every day over the past year and two months?

Yeah… I mean, it’s been around for about a year and two months. It kind of started after I graduated high school, when I was starting college classes and working full-time at the clinic.

I remember thinking it was just because everything changed all at once, and I was trying to get into a routine, but… it just kept going. Like even when I’d get a new planner or decide I was going to “get it together,” it didn’t really change that much.
Have you had at least two years where you felt this way, even if it wasn't every single day?

No, not two years. It’s been more like… about a year and two months.

It started after I graduated high school, when I was trying to do college classes and work full-time at the clinic, and I remember thinking maybe I was just overwhelmed because my schedule was all over the place. Like I’d be in class mode and then work mode, and I kept buying coffee from the same place near campus even though it was way too expensive… sorry, that’s not really the point.

But yeah, not two years. About a year and two months.
Have you experienced significant anxiety on most days for the past six months?

I’m not really sure… I mean, I get stressed, like with classes and work and just trying to keep everything straight, but I don’t know if I’d call it significant anxiety most days.

Like sometimes I’ll feel wound up, especially if I’m running late or I forgot something stupid like my badge or my charger, and then I’ll spiral about how unprepared I am… but I haven’t really been tracking it as “anxiety,” if that makes sense. So I guess I’m not sure if it’s been most days for six months.
